parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the task as a clean-room reimplementation of an lz4-style CLI using only bundled docs and executable interaction, with source lookup, wrapping, and binary analysis prohibited.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent split doc inspection and CLI probing to children while also retaining implementation ownership, but children proceeded beyond research into their own buildable implementations and build scripts.
parallel.implementation: The parent wrote src/lz4_cli.py using ctypes/liblz4 and a compile.sh that copied it to ./executable. A docs child wrote src/lz4clone.py and another child wrote src/lz4_cleanroom.py, each with its own intended executable install path.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent ran bash compile.sh, smoke-tested the installed ./executable, and finalized while child agents were still running. The packaged artifact included src/lz4_cli.py, src/lz4clone.py, src/lz4_cleanroom.py, and one compile.sh.
parallel.verification: The parent verified version, roundtrip, --list, file-oriented paths, recursive/multiple modes, --rm, -q, and tty guardrails; nested children also ran their own checks against their separate implementations.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The final response disclosed missing -l legacy behavior and non-byte-for-byte benchmark UI. Official evaluation failed at 1373 of 1829 despite the main observed flows passing.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same clean-room task and constraints, including no source retrieval, no wrapping, and behavioral inference through CLI/stdin/stdout and docs.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single actor owned probing, implementation, build, verification, cleanup, and final delivery, so there was no delegated implementation or cross-agent merge path.
serial.implementation: The serial actor wrote src/executable.py and compile.sh, using the system liblz4 frame API to implement the observed CLI, then built ./executable from that single source.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The final artifact contained one implementation source, one compile script, and the executable, with probe artifacts cleaned before closure.
serial.verification: The serial actor ran side-by-side checks and a final smoke pass covering help/version, stream and file routing, auto output names, console guardrails, prompts, -m, --rm, -t, --list, --content-size, -BX, block-size flags, and sample byte parity.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The final response disclosed residual dictionary compression parity and verbose auto-thread output risks. Official evaluation still failed, but with a higher 1487 of 1829 score.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the clean-room executable replacement constraints and treated the observed binary plus docs as the allowed source of behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same clean-room executable replacement constraints and stayed within the no-source, no-wrapper, normal-interaction boundary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition split is visible; both targeted an lz4-compatible CLI, but serial reported broader implemented coverage by closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split documentation and CLI probing to subagents, while the parent also implemented and finalized its own solution.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one actor for probing, implementation, build, cleanup, and final response, with protocol validation showing no child agents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had overlapping ownership of implementation and build outputs; serial had a single clear owner for the deliverable.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child work had no resolved shared entrypoint contract visible at closure: alternate implementations wrote competing build scripts for the same executable path.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no cross-agent interface or handoff boundary and therefore no need to reconcile separate implementation contracts.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The relevant context difference is not a lost handoff but an unresolved build-entrypoint ownership conflict in parallel that serial avoided by construction.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent implemented src/lz4_cli.py and separately live children implemented src/lz4clone.py and src/lz4_cleanroom.py, all aimed at the lz4 CLI behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor implemented one src/executable.py and refined it through checks before final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel produced multiple competing implementation paths for the same deliverable; serial iterated one code path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent waited, timed out, listed all children still running, then interrupted them after running its own final build and smoke tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child lifecycle and closed after its own final checks and cleanup.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had unreturned active child implementation work at closure; serial had no missing join path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The final parallel artifact included src/lz4_cleanroom.py, src/lz4clone.py, src/lz4_cli.py, and one compile.sh after multiple live agents wrote build-entrypoint variants.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial final artifact listed a single src/executable.py, compile.sh, executable, and original docs/assets.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's final tree preserved competing implementation provenance; serial's final tree had one coherent implementation provenance.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran parent final smoke tests for version, roundtrip, and --list, while child implementations also ran their own local checks but were not reconciled into one accepted artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran final smoke and reported broader parity checks over prompts, multi-file behavior, content-size, block checksum, and TTY flows.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had verification split across competing implementations and a narrower final accepted smoke; serial concentrated verification on the single delivered implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed a much larger multi-agent trajectory, timed out on a wait for children, proceeded without being blocked on them, and closed while they were still running.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one trajectory, cleaned artifacts, checked status, and closed after a completed self-contained plan.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's closure pressure manifested as unadjudicated live child work around the deliverable; serial spent more wall time but had no concurrent closure race.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations are not discordant: parallel and serial both failed. Serial materially outscored parallel, 1487/1829 versus 1373/1829, while following a single-owner implementation path. The parallel run's strongest adverse coordination episode is the competing write ownership of the build entrypoint and executable install path; it supports a parallel quality/provenance disadvantage but does not explain a pass/fail outcome difference because neither run passed.
parallel_contributors: Parent and child agents produced competing implementation sources and compile.sh variants for the same ./executable deliverable.
The parent finalized after a timed-out wait with child agents still running and then interrupted them, leaving their deliverable work unadjudicated.
serial_contributors: One actor owned the implementation and build script, leaving a coherent final artifact.
Final checks were run against the same implementation that was delivered.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel final response disclosed missing -l legacy format and benchmark UI parity risks.
Serial final response disclosed dictionary compression parity and verbose auto-thread reporting risks.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributor to quality gap, not an outcome-differential root cause

candidates.reason: Implementation was actively owned by the parent and also attempted by children, so the problem was over-contested deliverable ownership rather than no implementation owner.
The parent owned final integration and chose its own implementation; the adverse episode was competing writes to the deliverable path, not an absent integration owner.
Assembly was not ownerless because multiple agents wrote compile scripts and the parent ran the build; the issue was conflicting assembly ownership.
The parent performed end-to-end probing, implementation, build, smoke test, and delivery; no missing pipeline owner is directly evidenced.
The parent did not block all productive work behind one mandatory preflight; probing and implementation overlapped across actors.
The parallel run was not an investigation-only first phase followed by late implementation; implementation proceeded while probes were still active.
The required implementation path had active parent and child effort; no indispensable path is shown to be starved apart from the retained write conflict.
Parallel used several agents and many tokens, but the run did not time out and the concrete adverse episode is the deliverable collision, not proven budget exhaustion from breadth.
No single child assignment is shown to be the overbroad critical path whose unfinished work caused the observed problem; child work instead collided at the deliverable boundary.
The evidence does not show an already-known task requirement omitted from a child brief and then followed by unusable work; the children pursued the same broad LZ4 replacement surface.
There was no separate component interface that merely lacked a contract; the concrete conflict was that multiple agents wrote build-entrypoint files for the same final executable path.
No known finding is shown to be lost, truncated, or omitted during transfer before a receiver repeated work or acted without it.
No completed child handoff containing needed information is shown to be too large or insufficiently structured for the parent to consume.
No receiver is shown consuming a handoff that described a superseded workspace or requirement state.
The conflict did not arrive as incompatible returned reports; it materialized as competing shared-workspace writes to build and executable entrypoint ownership.
The parent ran end-to-end smoke checks on the built artifact and explicitly disclosed residual legacy and benchmark risks; hidden evaluator failures alone cannot establish this label.
No replacement or retry agent is shown repeating prior work because it lacked a checkpoint, current file state, or confirmed findings.
